content.text:
I've traced every responsive location. Summary of findings before submitting:

- **§9.4 (p0041)**: Customer may terminate the Agreement **or any Order Form** without cause; owes only accrued Fees; Vendor refunds prepaid Fees for the post-termination period.
- **§29.4 (p0122)**: the cross-referenced notice period is **thirty days** — satisfies the ≤30-day preferred element.
- **§10.2 (p0045)**: reinforces refund of prepaid recurring Fees for the period after termination.
- **Vendor exit rights**: §9 gives Vendor only cause-based rights (9.1 material breach, 9.2 insolvency); §13.1 bars licence suspension except for uncured payment/use breach; §24.4 bars termination on change of control. No Vendor convenience right anywhere.
- **No early-termination fee / clawback**: nothing in §7, §8 or §10 accelerates or claws back Fees on convenience termination (§7.7 is a late-payment charge, a payment-terms issue, not a convenience penalty). §2.1 confirms no minimum commitment.
- Noted only: §1.5 defines "Fees" as the Implementation Fee, which narrows the reach of the refund wording — a defined-term scope point, not a failure of a T4C material term (the fallback has no refund element at all).

All four preferred elements are met, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
input.rationale: This sits at our preferred position, so we are not redlining it. Section 9.4 gives us a convenience right over both the Agreement and any Order Form; chasing the cross-reference, Section 29.4 fixes the notice period at "thirty days before the effective termination date", i.e. within our 30-day preferred limit, and Sections 9.4 and 10.2 both require Vendor to refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination. There is no early-termination fee, clawback or Implementation Fee acceleration anywhere in Sections 7, 8 or 10 (Section 7.7 is a late-payment charge, addressed under the payment-terms rule, not a convenience penalty), and Section 2.1 confirms no minimum purchase commitment. Vendor has no mirror convenience right during the three-year term in Section 8.1: Section 9 gives Vendor only cause-based rights (9.1 material breach, 9.2 insolvency), Section 13.1 bars licence suspension except for an uncured payment or use breach, and Section 24.4 denies Vendor any right to terminate on our change of control. One drafting point we note but do not flag here: Section 1.5 defines "Fees" as the Implementation Fee only, which narrows the reach of the refund language against prepaid subscription charges; that is a defined-term scope issue for the fees rule, and the fallback for this rule imposes no refund requirement at all.
